Role Title:  Federal Budget Analyst   Role Type:  Contractor   Location:  Remote   micro1  is engaging Federal Budget Analysts to contribute to a customer's project focused on budget formulation and execution within the federal sector. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input.   Scope of Work  
 Create realistic training examples of federal budget justification materials, including narratives, exhibits, and supporting analyses. 
 Write sample responses to OMB passback with clear, well-supported analysis, and annotate the reasoning behind each choice. 
 Document mid-year reprogramming scenarios, noting which actions require higher-level approval and how they stay consistent with spend plans. 
 Build worked examples that compare actual expenditures against planned obligations, evaluate fund availability, and explain variances. 
 Walk through year-end closeout step by step, including reconciliation with accounting records and resolution of discrepancies. 
 Write guidance on funding types, budget changes, and compliance requirements, drawing on how experienced analysts advise program managers. 
 Produce templates, process walkthroughs, and annotated examples that capture how federal budget work is actually done. 
 Review AI-generated budget content for accuracy, realism, and compliance, and explain what is wrong or missing so it can be corrected. 
  Preferred Qualifications  
 5+ years of federal budget experience at about the GS-11/12 level or higher, in GS-0560, 0501, 0510, or comparable roles. 
 Experience with budget formulation, execution, and funds control. 
 Experience with OMB submissions, reprogramming, and year-end closeout. 
 Familiarity with federal accounting and budget execution systems. 
 Financial management certification (DoD FM, CGFM, or similar) a plus.

jobs.description:
Role Title:  Finance Research Expert   Role Type:  Contract   Location:  Remote  Required Skills:  
  Equity Research  
  FP&A  
  Corporate Finance  
  Accounting or Audit  
  Investor Relations  
  Credit Analysis  
  Opportunity Snapshot:  
   Time per task:  around 4 to 8 hours  
   Location:  Remote, worldwide  
   You’ll need:  Hands-on experience reading US SEC filings and familiarity with US GAAP  
   Your tasks:  Write finance research questions with a verified, sourced answer, and check each one against what AI models answer  
  Scope of Work:  
  You will work on questions about real US public companies. Each question points to information that sits in long filings or IR materials, or that requires comparing several of them to find the right answer.  
  Write questions that require finding a specific figure in a 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, proxy statement, earnings release or investor presentation.  
  Write questions where two documents show different numbers and the answer depends on knowing which one is correct (for example, original vs. restated figures, or adjusted vs. reported).  
  Pay attention to period and document version: the right fiscal year, the right filing, the latest amended version.  
  Test each question against current AI models and keep only the ones they answer incorrectly.  
  Rewrite questions when the wording allows more than one valid answer.  
  What we’re looking for:  
  Hands-on work with US filings in one of these backgrounds:   
  Equity research or investment analysis (sell-side or buy-side) covering US companies. Investment banking or corporate development. (M&A, equity capital markets), with experience in deal filings, prospectuses, ownership history and subsidiary structures.  
  Credit or restructuring analysis, with experience in credit agreements, bond terms and bankruptcy filings.  
  SEC reporting or audit. (Big 4 audit, corporate reporting), with experience in restatements, footnotes and how figures change across filings.  
  Corporate law or due diligence. (Securities law, KYC, investigations), with experience tracing entities, executives and related parties across records.  
  You should also be comfortable reading long filings, including footnotes and tables, and have clear written English.  
  How the selection process works:  
  Apply with your resume and a short profile.  
  Complete the finance interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with US filings and financial reporting. You don’t need to prepare or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.  
  Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.  
  Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.  
  Originally posted on  Himalayas

We're looking for professionals with hands-on experience in corporate development, acquisition evaluation, and M&A execution who can translate real-world financial expertise into rigorous AI evaluation frameworks.    What You'll Be Doing   
  Design and develop evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and scoring methodologies for AI agents operating in corporate development and M&A workflows.  
  Create realistic test cases covering acquisition screening, valuation, financial due diligence, deal structuring, and strategic investment decisions.  
  Evaluate AI-generated financial analyses, valuation models, acquisition assessments, and investment recommendations.  
  Translate real-world M&A experience into structured datasets, research scenarios, and measurable evaluation criteria.  
  Collaborate with AI researchers, engineers, and product teams to identify model limitations and improve financial reasoning capabilities.  
  Conduct applied research and document findings to advance AI performance in corporate finance and acquisition-related tasks.  
   What We're Looking For   
  Strong professional experience in Corporate Development, M&A, Investment Banking, Private Equity, or Strategic Investments, with direct exposure to acquisition-related transactions.  
  Hands-on experience across the M&A lifecycle, including target screening, valuation, due diligence, transaction analysis, or deal execution.  
  Strong understanding of acquisition strategies, financial modeling, company valuation (DCF, comparables, precedent transactions), and strategic fit assessments.  
  Experience preparing or evaluating investment memoranda, acquisition recommendations, and transaction-related financial analyses.  
  Ability to translate complex financial workflows into structured research questions, evaluation frameworks, and measurable criteria.  
  Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across technical and non-technical teams.  
  Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Accounting, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.  
   Preferred Qualifications   
  Direct experience within an in-house Corporate Development team, particularly involving buy-side acquisitions.

  Background in technology-sector acquisitions, SaaS businesses, or strategic investments.  
  MBA, CFA, or relevant advanced financial qualifications.  
  Familiarity with AI agents, large language models, AI evaluation methodologies, or financial AI applications.
